verdict.tagline: A grand Jedi adventure burdened by technical friction and mandatory launchers.
for_you_if: you want a sprawling lightsaber combat journey
you can overlook navigation hurdles across alien worlds
not_for_you_if: you will not install a third-party launcher
you need stable frame rates on release hardware
you mind backtracking without fast travel

distortion_flags.sentence: Reviews become steadily more positive as playtime increases past the initial hours.

claims.claim: Climbing mechanics and animations can trap the player or cause them to get stuck until falling.

citations.review_text:
You can certainly have fun with it, but personally, all that excessive climbing combined with the terrible controls just isn't worth my sanity. I kept getting stuck half way in pipes, and the climbing animations repeatedly left me unable to move, until the game mercifully let me plummet to my death so I could restart. I was so confused and frustrated by this that I reinstalled the entire game, which took ages due to my slow internet connection.
When it still didn't work after that, I hardly felt like this is worth it.
So I was stuck with a mechanic, that I already don't like and now it is also broken and causes me to loose health constantly.
I’ve read that the entire climbing thing doesn't really change as the game progresses, so I’d rather save myself the time and money and skip it altogether.

The Metroidvania style progression and exploration system doesn't really work here, either. Movement feels on rails for most mechanics, and aside from the exploration itself, I hardly got to utilize any of it, so what is the point?

I actually liked the combat system, though I barely got to experience it since I spent most of my time climbing or getting stuck while climbing.

The game certainly has its target audience, but I can't overlook the issues I had with it so, even as a Star Wars fan, I’m not part of that audience.

I am a recent fan of the Star Wars movies and I also recently discovered this game. What a wonderful introduction to the Star Wars gaming world. I really love this game. It is outside of my usual comfort zone, which is management and simulation games.

If you are a fan of adventure type games where you attack enemies, climb a lot, and have a good storyline, this game is for you!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking a fast-travel system, which makes backtracking through planets to return to the ship tedious and frustrating.

citations.review_text:
An awesome game overall that I would absolutely recommend, especially if you are a Star Wars fan. The story is captivating and the gameplay is fast-paced.
The combat is really nice as well; the lightsaber mechanics feel great, leaning slightly into a Souls-like combat system (fights are very satisfying). Visually, the game is superb. The graphics are great, and it runs really well on PC. 
Another huge plus is the diversity of the planets you visit, constantly changing biomes and atmospheres to keep the experience fresh. 
The only major flaw is that going back to the ship is really annoying. The game uses a Metroidvania structure but completely lacks a fast-travel system. Having to walk all the way back through the map to reach your ship gets frustrating sometimes tbh. 
There are no paywalls or anything, and the hidden chests you find are just for cosmetics.

Fantastic solo experience, makes me want to buy the sequel, Survivor.
8/10 couldve been a 9 if they added fast travel instead of making you walk the entire map after a mission

Pros
* Deep, challenging lightsaber combat heavily inspired by Sekiro, featuring rewarding parry mechanics and dynamic Force abilities.
* Masterful Metroid-vania level design that rewards thorough exploration with hidden upgrades, health expansions, and cosmetic custom cosmetics.
* Compelling, canonical Star Wars narrative that successfully captures the dark, oppressive atmosphere of the galaxy following Order 66.
* Spectacular cinematic set pieces, colossal boss battles, and a sweeping orchestral soundtrack that feels authentic to the films.
* Features a rich lineup of memorable characters including Cal Kestis, BD-1, Cere Junda, Greez Dritus, Saw Gerrera, Tarfful, Jaro Tapal, Prauf, Second Sister (Trilla Suduri), Ninth Sister, Taron Malicos, Merrin, and Darth Vader.

Cons
* Complete lack of a fast-travel system forces players into long, highly tedious stretches of backtracking through massive planets to return to their ship.
* Map navigation can feel incredibly frustrating due to a confusing, cluttered 3D Holomap layout that is difficult to read.
* Periodic technical issues, including stuttering, slow texture loading, and awkward character animations during platforming sequences.
* Lightsaber custom choices are entirely cosmetic, providing no mechanical advantages, stat boosts, or gameplay variety.

Overall, I rate the game highly, praising it as a triumphant return to high-quality single-player Star Wars games. While players frequently express frustration over the tedious backtracking and clunky platforming physics, the community agrees that the superb combat, satisfying exploration, and strong narrative make it a must-play for fans of the franchise.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Longer-term players continue highlighting map navigation hurdles and mandatory external launcher requirements.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that navigating the levels and maps can be frustrating, and note that the game lacks a fast travel system.

citations.review_text:
As a huge Star Wars nerd and Dark Souls fan, I was really excited to play this game. While I enjoyed it overall, it falls short in a few areas.

The collectibles are plentiful, but they don't feel rewarding enough. Unlocking new weapons, combat moves, or meaningful upgrades instead of mostly cosmetic items would have made exploration much more satisfying.

The locations are beautifully designed, but the map doesn't do them justice. Navigation can be frustrating, and the game really needed a way to place custom markers or fast travel back to mantis.

Overall, I'd give it a 7.5/10. The game had a lot of potential, but a few design choices kept it from being truly great.

Definitely among the best Star Wars games that have come out in a long time. Gameplay and story are both excellent. Soundtrack is also fairly good. 

My main complaint is that the levels can sometimes feel like a giant maze and it's tedious to find your way around in them after the level is complete, even with the help of the in-game map. 

It also would have been nice if they added an optional VR mode to play it in a VR headset with 3D graphics (using the normal Xbox controller, not VR motion controllers).  Similar games like "Edge of Nowhere" have done this before and it worked well, so it's sad to see it's not an option with this game.

Despite these flaws, it's still excellent and easy to recommend.

A great game overall. Some of the maps can be a bit confusing especially if you want to get to a certain spot - especially the ones with multiple levels.
